195: /// Removes surrounding quotes from a string. Doesn't remove quotes from raw
196: /// strings. Returns the original string if it doesn't have matching quotes.
197: fn remove_quotes(s: &str) -> &str {
198:     let quoted_by_double_quotes = s.len() >= 2 && s.starts_with('"') && s.ends_with('"');
199:     let quoted_by_single_quotes = s.len() >= 2 && s.starts_with('\'') && s.ends_with('\'');
200:     let quoted_by_backticks = s.len() >= 2 && s.starts_with('`') && s.ends_with('`');
201:     if quoted_by_double_quotes || quoted_by_single_quotes || quoted_by_backticks {
202:         &s[1..s.len() - 1]
203:     } else {
204:         s
205:     }
206: }

208: /// Evaluate all arguments from a call, performing expansions when necessary.
209: pub fn eval_arguments_from_call(
210:     engine_state: &EngineState,
211:     stack: &mut Stack,
212:     call: &Call,
213: ) -> Result<Vec<Spanned<String>>, ShellError> {
214:     let cwd = engine_state.cwd(Some(stack))?;
215:     let mut args: Vec<Spanned<String>> = vec![];
216:     for (expr, spread) in call.rest_iter(1) {
217:         if is_bare_string(expr) {
218:             // If `expr` is a bare string, perform tilde-expansion,
219:             // glob-expansion, and inner-quotes-removal, in that order.
220:             for arg in eval_argument(engine_state, stack, expr, spread)? {
221:                 let tilde_expanded = expand_tilde(&arg);
222:                 for glob_expanded in expand_glob(&tilde_expanded, &cwd, expr.span)? {
223:                     let inner_quotes_removed = remove_inner_quotes(&glob_expanded);
224:                     args.push(inner_quotes_removed.into_owned().into_spanned(expr.span));
225:                 }
226:             }
227:         } else {
228:             for arg in eval_argument(engine_state, stack, expr, spread)? {
229:                 args.push(arg.into_spanned(expr.span));
230:             }
231:         }
232:     }
233:     Ok(args)
234: }

236: /// Evaluates an expression, coercing the values to strings.
237: ///
238: /// Note: The parser currently has a special hack that retains surrounding
239: /// quotes for string literals in `Expression`, so that we can decide whether
240: /// the expression is considered a bare string. The hack doesn't affect string
241: /// literals within lists or records. This function will remove the quotes
242: /// before evaluating the expression.
243: fn eval_argument(
244:     engine_state: &EngineState,
245:     stack: &mut Stack,
246:     expr: &Expression,
247:     spread: bool,
248: ) -> Result<Vec<String>, ShellError> {
249:     // Remove quotes from string literals.
250:     let mut expr = expr.clone();
251:     if let Expr::String(s) = &expr.expr {
252:         expr.expr = Expr::String(remove_quotes(s).into());
253:     }
254: 
255:     let eval = get_eval_expression(engine_state);
256:     match eval(engine_state, stack, &expr)? {
257:         Value::List { vals, .. } => {
258:             if spread {
259:                 vals.into_iter()
260:                     .map(|val| val.coerce_into_string())
261:                     .collect()
262:             } else {
263:                 Err(ShellError::CannotPassListToExternal {
264:                     arg: String::from_utf8_lossy(engine_state.get_span_contents(expr.span)).into(),
265:                     span: expr.span,
266:                 })
267:             }
268:         }
269:         value => {
270:             if spread {
271:                 Err(ShellError::CannotSpreadAsList { span: expr.span })
272:             } else {
273:                 Ok(vec![value.coerce_into_string()?])
274:             }
275:         }
276:     }
277: }

279: /// Returns whether an expression is considered a bare string.
280: ///
281: /// Bare strings are defined as string literals that are either unquoted or
282: /// quoted by backticks. Raw strings or string interpolations don't count.
283: fn is_bare_string(expr: &Expression) -> bool {
284:     let Expr::String(s) = &expr.expr else {
285:         return false;
286:     };
287:     let quoted_by_double_quotes = s.len() >= 2 && s.starts_with('"') && s.ends_with('"');
288:     let quoted_by_single_quotes = s.len() >= 2 && s.starts_with('\'') && s.ends_with('\'');
289:     !quoted_by_double_quotes && !quoted_by_single_quotes
290: }

575: /// Transforms `--option="value"` into `--option=value`. `value` can be quoted
576: /// with double quotes, single quotes, or backticks. Only removes the outermost
577: /// pair of quotes after the equal sign.
578: fn remove_inner_quotes(arg: &str) -> Cow<'_, str> {
579:     // Check that `arg` is a long option.
580:     if !arg.starts_with("--") {
581:         return Cow::Borrowed(arg);
582:     }
583:     // Split `arg` on the first `=`.
584:     let Some((option, value)) = arg.split_once('=') else {
585:         return Cow::Borrowed(arg);
586:     };
587:     // Check that `option` doesn't contain quotes.
588:     if option.contains('"') || option.contains('\'') || option.contains('`') {
589:         return Cow::Borrowed(arg);
590:     }
591:     // Remove the outermost pair of quotes from `value`.
592:     let value = remove_quotes(value);
593:     Cow::Owned(format!("{option}={value}"))
594: }

596: /// Write `PipelineData` into `writer`. If `PipelineData` is not binary, it is
597: /// first rendered using the `table` command.
598: ///
599: /// Note: Avoid using this function when piping data from an external command to
600: /// another external command, because it copies data unnecessarily. Instead,
601: /// extract the pipe from the `PipelineData::ByteStream` of the first command
602: /// and hand it to the second command directly.
603: fn write_pipeline_data(
604:     mut engine_state: EngineState,
605:     mut stack: Stack,
606:     data: PipelineData,
607:     mut writer: impl Write,
608: ) -> Result<(), ShellError> {
609:     if let PipelineData::ByteStream(stream, ..) = data {
610:         stream.write_to(writer)?;
611:     } else if let PipelineData::Value(Value::Binary { val, .. }, ..) = data {
612:         writer.write_all(&val)?;
613:     } else {
614:         stack.start_capture();
615: 
616:         // Turn off color as we pass data through
617:         Arc::make_mut(&mut engine_state.config).use_ansi_coloring = false;
618: 
619:         // Invoke the `table` command.
620:         let output =
621:             crate::Table.run(&engine_state, &mut stack, &Call::new(Span::unknown()), data)?;
622: 
623:         // Write the output.
624:         for value in output {
625:             let bytes = value.coerce_into_binary()?;
626:             writer.write_all(&bytes)?;
627:         }
628:     }
629:     Ok(())
630: }

632: /// Returns a helpful error message given an invalid command name,
633: pub fn command_not_found(
634:     name: &str,
635:     span: Span,
636:     engine_state: &EngineState,
637:     stack: &mut Stack,
638: ) -> ShellError {
639:     // Run the `command_not_found` hook if there is one.
640:     if let Some(hook) = &engine_state.config.hooks.command_not_found {
641:         let mut stack = stack.start_capture();
642:         // Set a special environment variable to avoid infinite loops when the
643:         // `command_not_found` hook triggers itself.
644:         let canary = "ENTERED_COMMAND_NOT_FOUND";
645:         if stack.has_env_var(engine_state, canary) {
646:             return ShellError::ExternalCommand {
647:                 label: format!(
648:                     "Command {name} not found while running the `command_not_found` hook"
649:                 ),
650:                 help: "Make sure the `command_not_found` hook itself does not use unknown commands"
651:                     .into(),
652:                 span,
653:             };
654:         }
655:         stack.add_env_var(canary.into(), Value::bool(true, Span::unknown()));
656: 
657:         let output = eval_hook(
658:             &mut engine_state.clone(),
659:             &mut stack,
660:             None,
661:             vec![("cmd_name".into(), Value::string(name, span))],
662:             hook,
663:             "command_not_found",
664:         );
665: 
666:         // Remove the special environment variable that we just set.
667:         stack.remove_env_var(engine_state, canary);
668: 
669:         match output {
670:             Ok(PipelineData::Value(Value::String { val, .. }, ..)) => {
671:                 return ShellError::ExternalCommand {
672:                     label: format!("Command `{name}` not found"),
673:                     help: val,
674:                     span,
675:                 };
676:             }
677:             Err(err) => {
678:                 return err;
679:             }
680:             _ => {
681:                 // The hook did not return a string, so ignore it.
682:             }
683:         }
684:     }
685: 
686:     // If the name is one of the removed commands, recommend a replacement.
687:     if let Some(replacement) = crate::removed_commands().get(&name.to_lowercase()) {
688:         return ShellError::RemovedCommand {
689:             removed: name.to_lowercase(),
690:             replacement: replacement.clone(),
691:             span,
692:         };
693:     }
694: 
695:     // The command might be from another module. Try to find it.
696:     if let Some(module) = engine_state.which_module_has_decl(name.as_bytes(), &[]) {
697:         let module = String::from_utf8_lossy(module);
698:         // Is the command already imported?
699:         let full_name = format!("{module} {name}");
700:         if engine_state.find_decl(full_name.as_bytes(), &[]).is_some() {
701:             return ShellError::ExternalCommand {
702:                 label: format!("Command `{name}` not found"),
703:                 help: format!("Did you mean `{full_name}`?"),
704:                 span,
705:             };
706:         } else {
707:             return ShellError::ExternalCommand {
708:                 label: format!("Command `{name}` not found"),
709:                 help: format!("A command with that name exists in module `{module}`. Try importing it with `use`"),
710:                 span,
711:             };
712:         }
713:     }
714: 
715:     // Try to match the name with the search terms of existing commands.
716:     let signatures = engine_state.get_signatures(false);
717:     if let Some(sig) = signatures.iter().find(|sig| {
718:         sig.search_terms
719:             .iter()
720:             .any(|term| term.to_folded_case() == name.to_folded_case())
721:     }) {
722:         return ShellError::ExternalCommand {
723:             label: format!("Command `{name}` not found"),
724:             help: format!("Did you mean `{}`?", sig.name),
725:             span,
726:         };
727:     }
728: 
729:     // Try a fuzzy search on the names of all existing commands.
730:     if let Some(cmd) = did_you_mean(signatures.iter().map(|sig| &sig.name), name) {
731:         // The user is invoking an external command with the same name as a
732:         // built-in command. Remind them of this.
733:         if cmd == name {
734:             return ShellError::ExternalCommand {
735:                 label: format!("Command `{name}` not found"),
736:                 help: "There is a built-in command with the same name".into(),
737:                 span,
738:             };
739:         }
740:         return ShellError::ExternalCommand {
741:             label: format!("Command `{name}` not found"),
742:             help: format!("Did you mean `{cmd}`?"),
743:             span,
744:         };
745:     }
746: 
747:     // We found nothing useful. Give up and return a generic error message.
748:     ShellError::ExternalCommand {
749:         label: format!("Command `{name}` not found"),
750:         help: format!("`{name}` is neither a Nushell built-in or a known external command"),
751:         span,
752:     }

758: /// This is a wrapper around `which::which_in()` except that, on Windows, it
759: /// also searches the current directory before any PATH entries.
760: ///
761: /// Note: the `which.rs` crate always uses PATHEXT from the environment. As
762: /// such, changing PATHEXT within Nushell doesn't work without updating the
763: /// actual environment of the Nushell process.
764: pub fn which(name: &str, paths: &str, cwd: &Path) -> Option<PathBuf> {

770: /// Returns true if `name` is a (somewhat useful) CMD internal command. The full
771: /// list can be found at https://ss64.com/nt/syntax-internal.html
772: fn is_cmd_internal_command(name: &str) -> bool {
773:     const COMMANDS: &[&str] = &[
774:         "ASSOC", "CLS", "ECHO", "FTYPE", "MKLINK", "PAUSE", "START", "VER", "VOL",
775:     ];
776:     COMMANDS.iter().any(|cmd| cmd.eq_ignore_ascii_case(name))
777: }

779: /// Returns true if a string contains CMD special characters.
780: #[cfg(windows)]
781: fn has_cmd_special_character(s: &str) -> bool {
782:     const SPECIAL_CHARS: &[char] = &['<', '>', '&', '|', '^'];
783:     SPECIAL_CHARS.iter().any(|c| s.contains(*c))
784: }

786: /// Escape an argument for CMD internal commands. The result can be safely
787: /// passed to `raw_arg()`.
788: #[cfg(windows)]
789: fn escape_cmd_argument(arg: &Spanned<String>) -> Result<Cow<'_, str>, ShellError> {
790:     let Spanned { item: arg, span } = arg;
791:     if arg.contains('"') {
792:         // If `arg` is already quoted by double quotes, confirm there's no
793:         // embedded double quotes, then leave it as is.
794:         if arg.chars().filter(|c| *c == '"').count() == 2
795:             && arg.starts_with('"')
796:             && arg.ends_with('"')
797:         {
798:             Ok(Cow::Borrowed(arg))
799:         } else {
800:             Err(ShellError::ExternalCommand {
801:                 label: "Arguments to CMD internal commands cannot contain embedded double quotes"
802:                     .into(),
803:                 help: "CMD doesn't support escaping double quotes inside double quotes".into(),
804:                 span: *span,
805:             })
806:         }
807:     } else if arg.contains(' ') || has_cmd_special_character(arg) {
808:         // If `arg` contains space or special characters, quote the entire argument by double quotes.
809:         Ok(Cow::Owned(format!("\"{arg}\"")))
810:     } else {
811:         Ok(Cow::Borrowed(arg))
812:     }
813: }
